chunks: From him, from Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzaal and Al-hajjaal, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said:

A man from the Ajaliyya heard this hadith: A caller will call out, 'So-and-so son of so-and-so and his Shites are the successful ones' at the beginning of the day, and another will call out at the end of the day, 'Uthman and his Shites are the successful ones.' He said: 'And the caller at the beginning of the day is the caller of the end of the day.' So the man said, 'So what makes us understand which one is the truthful from the liar?'
He said: 'The one who would believe in it before the call, would be ratifying it.'
Is He then Who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who himself does not go aright unless he is guided?

key_terms.آخِرَ النَّهَارِ: at the end of the day
key_terms.أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ: Is He then Who guides to the truth
key_terms.أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ: at the beginning of the day

ai.seo_question: How do we distinguish the truthful caller from the liar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of 'Ilm al-Badhi' (divinely granted prior knowledge) by contrasting those who recognize truth through innate conviction with those who require external validation. It highlights that true followers of the Ahl al-Bayt are identified by their pre-existing faith in the Imamate before the public proclamation, thereby distinguishing them from the general populace. The citation of Quran 10:35 reinforces the principle that the one who guides to the truth is inherently more worthy of emulation than the one who merely follows guidance.
